about: Feature patterns for motioncount.py --level N, and the places that move in a script, read at start. places: each match in a script (comments blanked, <style> blocks aside) is one place that moves: what animates, and a style that moves written in a script (styled or css templates, sx and style objects, <motion.div animate>, Svelte's transition:). Each feature is found when one of its signals matches in the app's own code. view: style (stylesheets and <style> blocks), script (scripts, components, <script> blocks), markup (tags and attributes). Comments never count; a match must start outside a string unless strings is true. rule: the match must be in the declarations of a rule whose selector this pattern finds ("" for any rule); a rule for an m- class counts once an element carries the class. also: a second pattern the same file must hold, outside strings. same_file_as: only in a file where that feature (an earlier one) was found. with: only once that feature (an earlier one) was found in some file. inside: only in a file of that feature, or inside an element, up to six levels up, that such a file mounts the scene on (the selector of its lazyScene( call, .hero-scene, #hero, [data-hero]; with no such call, any it selects) or defines as a component (<Scene>, or its file Scene.tsx; <hero-scene> and <x-hero> stand for HeroScene and Hero); or inside the component of a template that holds such an element (<x-hero> for hero.blade.php), or in a partial or component that template names, when it is inside no element of its own file.
ask: Ask the user how strong the look should be, 1 to 5 (python3 ../forge/level.py show look has the table), then record it: python3 ../forge/level.py set look N --said '<their words>'

features.name: a reduced-motion rule
features.needs: add @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) to the app's stylesheet, turning movement off or into a fade (motion.css has one)

features.name: an entrance (motion when the page loads)
features.needs: make the main content arrive: m-enter or m-stagger of motion.css on it, a keyframe animation of its own, @starting-style, or element.animate()

features.name: a page or view transition, or a counted number
features.needs: add a page transition (@view-transition { navigation: auto; }, startViewTransition(), <ViewTransition>) or a count-up (motion.md section 4)

features.name: scroll-driven motion
features.needs: add motion that follows the scroll: an IntersectionObserver reveal, animation-timeline: view(), or a sticky scene with story(), motion.md section 8

features.name: CSS 3D or the kit's depth.js
features.needs: add real depth: perspective with rotateX/rotateY on cards or panels, transform-style: preserve-3d, or the kit's depth.js (imported, data-depth on the cards)

features.name: a WebGL scene
features.needs: add a WebGL scene made for this app, on the screen that shows it: a kit scene through lazyScene, or three through the app's own package manager (motion.md section 5)

features.name: pointer input reaching the scene
features.needs: make the scene follow the pointer: a pointermove listener in the scene's file, setPointer(x, y), or a kit scene (its stage reads the pointer itself)

features.name: a fallback for no WebGL
features.needs: give the scene a still for no WebGL and reduced motion: data-scene-poster on it, in the container's template (up to six levels down), or a branch for no WebGL

features.name: a scroll journey through the scene
features.needs: build the journey with the kit's journey.js: chapters that move the camera through one scene (scenes.md section 6); setProgress alone is level 4's depth

features.name: a custom shader
features.needs: write a shader of the app's own: a ShaderMaterial (or RawShaderMaterial) in the app's code, on the kit's glsl.js (motion.md section 10); a kit scene alone is not one

features.name: a data hook
features.needs: feed the app's own data into the scene: scene.setData(values) or a uniform set from the data
